notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server MAY treat receipt of these frames in 0-RTT packets as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A client MUST discard a Version Negotiation packet that lists the QUIC version selected by the client.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: In response to an apparent migration, endpoints MUST validate the previously active path using a PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: To avoid a deadlock, a sender SHOULD ensure that other frames are sent periodically in addition to PADDING frames to elicit acknowledgments from the receiver.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MUST treat the receipt of a frame of unknown type as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a transport parameter with an invalid value as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: In QUIC version 1, this value MUST NOT exceed 20.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server MAY provide clients with an address validation token during one connection that can be used on a subsequent connection.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Endpoints MAY retire connection IDs containing patterns known to be problematic without using them.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MAY defer path validation until after a peer sends the next non-probing frame to its new address.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Application protocols that use QUIC SHOULD provide guidance on when deferring an idle timeout is appropriate.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server MUST NOT send more than one Retry packet in response to a single UDP datagram.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint that provides a zero-length connection ID MUST treat receipt of a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: For this reason, endpoints MAY discard packets rather than immediately close if errors are detected in packets that lack authentication.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: PADDING, PING, and CRYPTO frames MAY appear in any packet number space.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: The value in the Unused field is set to an arbitrary value by the server; a client MUST ignore these bits.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MAY also limit the issuance of connection IDs to reduce the amount of per-path state it maintains, such as path validation status, as its peer might interact with it over as many paths as there are issued connection IDs.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: To protect the connection from failing due to such a spurious migration, an endpoint MUST revert to using the last validated peer address when validation of a new peer address fails.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server MUST ensure that every NEW_TOKEN frame it sends is unique across all clients, with the exception of those sent to repair losses of previously sent NEW_TOKEN frames.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: The HANDSHAKE_DONE frame MUST be retransmitted until it is acknowledged.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A client MUST discard a Retry packet with a zero-length Retry Token field.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Receipt of a frame that exceeds this limit MUST be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR or FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Note that this mechanism does not protect against downgrade attacks and MUST NOT be used outside of draft implementations.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Senders MUST NOT send data in excess of either limit.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: While there are legitimate uses for all messages, implementations SHOULD track cost of processing relative to progress and treat excessive quantities of any non-productive packets as indicative of an attack.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MUST acknowledge all ack-eliciting Initial and Handshake packets immediately and all ack-eliciting 0-RTT and 1-RTT packets within its advertised max_ack_delay, with the following exception.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A client that migrates to a new address SHOULD use a preferred address from the same address family for the server.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server MUST treat receipt of a HANDSHAKE_DONE frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Upon detecting losses, a sender MUST take appropriate congestion control action.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: More generally, servers MUST NOT generate a stateless reset if a connection with the corresponding connection ID could be active on any endpoint using the same static key.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: The value for Source Connection ID MUST be copied from the Destination Connection ID of the received packet, which is initially randomly selected by a client.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint that detects an error SHOULD signal the existence of that error to its peer.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Endpoints that send data using IPv6 SHOULD apply an IPv6 flow label in compliance with [RFC6437], unless the local API does not allow setting IPv6 flow labels.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server MAY store and recover the previously sent values of the max_idle_timeout, max_udp_payload_size, and disable_active_migration parameters and reject 0-RTT if it selects smaller values.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Endpoints MAY choose to allow more data to be buffered during the handshake.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MUST NOT open more streams than permitted by the current stream limit set by its peer.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: The client MUST NOT use the token provided in a Retry for future connections.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server MUST NOT send more than one Version Negotiation packet in response to a single UDP datagram.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Because port-only changes are commonly the result of NAT rebinding or other middlebox activity, the endpoint MAY instead retain its congestion control state and round-trip estimate in those cases instead of reverting to initial values.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A receiver SHOULD include an ACK Range containing the largest received packet number in every ACK frame.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: To ensure simple and efficient implementations of frame parsing, a frame type MUST use the shortest possible encoding.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: If 0-RTT data is accepted by the server, the server MUST NOT reduce any limits or alter any values that might be violated by the client with its 0-RTT data.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server MAY abort the connection if it detects that the client reset the packet number.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Servers MAY communicate a preferred address of each address family (IPv4 and IPv6) to allow clients to pick the one most suited to their network attachment.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a packet that has a non-zero value for these bits, after removing both packet and header protection, as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Receivers SHOULD ignore any subsequent packets with a different Destination Connection ID than the first packet in the datagram.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Receipt of the same frame multiple times MUST NOT be treated as a connection error.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Endpoints SHOULD retire connection IDs when they are no longer actively using either the local or destination address for which the connection ID was used.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Tokens sent in NEW_TOKEN frames MUST include information that allows the server to verify that the client IP address has not changed from when the token was issued.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Clients MAY use tokens obtained on one connection for any connection attempt using the same version.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A client MUST discard a Retry packet that contains a Source Connection ID field that is identical to the Destination Connection ID field of its Initial packet.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint's selected connection ID and the QUIC version are sufficient information to identify packets for a closing connection; the endpoint MAY discard all other connection state.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Endpoints MAY choose to reduce the risk of request forgery by not including values from NEW_TOKEN frames in Initial packets or by only sending probing frames in packets prior to completing address validation.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A server that chooses a zero-length connection ID MUST NOT provide a preferred address.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Information that allows the server to distinguish between tokens from Retry and NEW_TOKEN MAY be accessible to entities other than the server.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint SHOULD NOT initiate migration with a peer that has requested a zero-length connection ID, because traffic over the new path might be trivially linkable to traffic over the old one.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Receivers MUST be able to process coalesced packets.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: Requests for multiple codepoints MAY use a contiguous range.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: The new connection MUST use a new random Destination Connection ID different from the one it had previously sent.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling application errors (type 0x1d) MUST only appear in the application data packet number space.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: To avoid excessively small idle timeout periods, endpoints MUST increase the idle timeout period to be at least three times the current Probe Timeout (PTO).
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: If any use of the codepoints is identified by this search or a request to update the registration is made, the codepoint MUST NOT be reclaimed.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A client MUST NOT send 0-RTT packets once it starts processing 1-RTT packets from the server.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: A client or server MAY advertise support for any of these reserved versions.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint SHOULD use a large enough packet number encoding to allow the packet number to be recovered even if the packet arrives after packets that are sent afterwards.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MAY skip packet numbers when sending packets to detect this behavior.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MUST NOT delay transmission of a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame unless constrained by congestion control.
notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

clause_text: An endpoint MAY skip validation of a peer address if that address has been seen recently.
